question: A 14-month-old child presents to a rural PHC with fast breathing (RR 46/min), chest in-drawing, and is unable to drink. The health worker correctly classifies cough/breathing. According to the IMNCI colour-coded triage system, which colour category applies, and what is the IMMEDIATE required action?

answers.text: Yellow — prescribe oral amoxicillin and advise the mother to return in 2 days.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Yellow (Some Pneumonia) requires home treatment with oral antibiotics, but chest in-drawing alone would classify as Yellow. Here, 'unable to drink' is a general danger sign — elevating the classification.

answers.text: Pink — refer urgently to hospital after giving pre-referral treatment (first dose of appropriate antibiotic + oxygen if available).

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. 'Unable to drink or breastfeed' is a general danger sign, which automatically triggers a Pink (Urgent Referral) classification regardless of other findings. Pre-referral treatment and urgent referral are mandatory.

answers.text: Green — reassure the mother and provide ORS; recheck in 5 days.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Green indicates a well child with no pneumonia or no dehydration. This child has a general danger sign and elevated respiratory rate — Green is inappropriate.

answers.text: Yellow — give the first dose of cotrimoxazole and refer to a secondary facility within 24 hours.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cotrimoxazole is not first-line for childhood pneumonia in the current IMNCI algorithm. More importantly, the presence of a general danger sign mandates immediate urgent referral — not a delayed referral.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the IMNCI colour-coded triage system. Pink (urgent referral) is triggered by any general danger sign. Here, 'unable to drink' is a general danger sign — it overrides any lower classification from the breathing domain alone.

Well done. The IMNCI override rule: any general danger sign (unable to drink/breastfeed, vomiting everything, convulsions, abnormally sleepy/unconscious) classifies the child as Pink regardless of other domain findings. Pre-referral treatment and urgent referral follow immediately.
